scope: remaining appearance/Effect authoring surface: optional held component exposure and explicit Clip Effect removal
invariants: Every optional held component the pure owner patches is reachable from the editor, and nothing else is: the audit maps owner capability to editor, admission ingress and route coverage in both directions.
Only independently dirty fields enter one patch; the component never clamps, normalizes, or substitutes a default for an absent component or a mixed span.

Closed discriminated components (presentation, blink) must reach the owner complete; an undirtied member falls back to its uniform authored value and a mixed or absent one is left incomplete for the owner to refuse.
Removal is one explicit owner-accepted null target, never a side effect of an empty draft.

Effect removal takes the Effect from the selected held stacks and exactly the Clip-owned clip-effect tracks whose activation intersects a span that no longer carries it, reported in affectedTrackIds/removedIds with their keyframes in affectedPropertyKeyIds.

Removal never touches another Clip's tracks, instance-target tracks, Group definitions, Group occurrences, pattern instances or any other held component; retained nonlinear curve descriptors survive byte-exact.
A surviving Transition property ramp on the removed Effect refuses the whole edit atomically, names the Transition and returns the original record identity.
Refusal and no-op return the original record with all fourteen affected collections empty, produce no history or save, and leave the intent object unmutated.
Timed Effect reordering keeps its existing refusal; no compiler or lowering capability is widened anywhere in this slice.
